title: Hybrid telemetry-driven region decider with asymmetric percentile gating and network-quality weighting
creator: Rajesh Kumar
description:
Objective: Build a region selection service that combines latency percentiles (p50, p95) with a separate network-quality score (packet loss/retx/jitter) to choose the best endpoint and trigger graceful fallback to compatible model variants.

Background: Current region selection uses single-metric percentile thresholds in several places; this leads to noisy switches during transient spikes and does not account for packet-level degradation that increases tail latency in unpredictable ways. We need a hybrid decision surface that: (1) uses asymmetric gating on p50 vs p95 depending on traffic class, (2) factors in network-quality signals as a multiplier/penalty, and (3) supports model-variant-aware fallback when the selected region is unhealthy.

Proposed design summary:
- Collect sliding-window p50 and p95 latency per POP and per model-variant (5m / 1m windows).
- Compute a network-quality score per POP from recent packet-loss percentage, jitter (ms), and retransmit rate; normalize into a 0..1 penalty where 1=healthy.
- Asymmetric percentile gating: for latency-sensitive routes (low timeout budgets), bias decision toward p50 (weighted 0.6 p50 / 0.4 p95); for high-throughput batch routes, bias toward p95 (0.3 p50 / 0.7 p95).
- Final POP score = latency_score * network_quality_penalty * tier_multiplier, where latency_score is a percentile-normalized value and tier_multiplier encodes customer tier preferences (e.g., premium customers get higher weighting for lower-latency POPs).
- Tie-breaker: prefer POP with warmer KV cache hit rate > 75% unless the other POP has 10% lower final score.
- Fallbacks: when POP final score crosses a safety threshold, automatically route to a queued compatible model-variant in the same or adjacent region (policy-configurable); emit an event and create trace links for postmortem.

Implementation notes:
- Telemetry sources: existing edge latency collectors (p50/p95 histograms), infra packet-metrics (tcptrace/flow logs), and KV-cache hitrate metrics from serving runtime.
- Scoring cadence: compute POP scores every 10s with exponential decay weights for sub-minute smoothing; allow fast path (1s) for critical routes flagged in route metadata.
- Config: expose policy knobs in Console: percentile weights, network penalty curve, safety threshold, and model-variant fallback priority list.

Success metrics: reduced unnecessary POP flips (target: <2 flips per hour per route during steady-state), improved p95 tail for priority customers by 5-10%, and reduced error rate on cross-region fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: POP scoring service returns stable ranked list for given route within 50ms of invocation
Configurable percentile weights applied per route class via Console
Network-quality penalty calculated from packet-loss/jitter/retransmit and validated against synthetic injection tests
Graceful model-variant fallback triggers and preserves request integrity for compatible variants (schema/attempts)
Dashboard shows flips, reason codes (latency/network/tier), and per-POP score breakdown
E2E canary shows <2 unintended region switches per hour and p95 improvement targets met for priority customers
comments: 2026-03-06 - Rajesh Kumar: Initial spike: added spec for asymmetric gating based on route metadata. Requested weigh-in from Network infra on penalty curve.

2026-03-08 - Miguel Santos (Network): Suggested using EWMA of packet-loss with 30s half-life to avoid reacting to single bad samples. Also recommended capping penalty to avoid blackholing a region during brief congestion.

2026-03-09 - Emily Chen: Prototype scorer implemented in scoring-service branch. Unit tests for percentile normalization added. Observed frequent oscillation in staging when using raw p95 — switched smoothing to 3-window median.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Aisha Patel): Console knobs UX sketched. Emphasized making safety threshold explicit and defaulting to 'conservative' for new routes.
2026-03-11 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/scoring-service/pull/412 - includes scoring, network-penalty, and config endpoints. Requesting code review from infra and runtime teams.

2026-03-12 - QA: Ran synthetic packet-loss injections against staging; network penalty behaved as expected but fallback ordering occasionally preferred adjacent region with cold KV cache — added KV hitrate tie-breaker to acceptance criteria.
